sources_admitted.evidence: 33 records pinned under data/sources/venezuela-oil and data/sources/coverage with text and hash; the State Department report is pinned from state.gov with a full Mistral OCR of its 53 pages because capture's OCR dropped the image pages holding the ledgers, and X posts and the USAspending award were admitted from saved files.

derived_numbers_computed.evidence: The vendor groups (health $57.4 million, oil, power, coal and fertilizer $35.6 million, service providers $28.8 million, international bodies $10.4 million) are sums of the report's 38-line vendor ledger, which itself sums to the stated $133,114,048.23; the five banks' 83% and Banco de Venezuela's $2.88 billion are sums of the report's three bank ledgers.

outlet_claims_verified.evidence: The Times' line that the $130 million in vendor payments went mostly to debts to other governments and international organizations was checked against the public ledger, which shows $10.4 million to such bodies; the page keeps the caveat that the Times read the confidential copy.

live_elements_guarded.evidence: The page has no live elements; every figure is as of September 30, 2026, the report's cutoff, and the page says the report may be updated.

subject_page_updated.evidence: The Venezuela oil subject page dek now carries the account's $12.26 billion and 98.7 percent paid out, with a new current figure for the share paid out, sourced to the report.
